newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil won't change coffee auction pace - grower.
newsitem.headline: Brazil won't change coffee auction pace - grower.

text.p: The Brazilian government won't change the pace and scope of its coffee stock sales unless market conditions make it necessary, given that coffee exports are progressing at a good rhythm, a grower representative said.

"Brazil is exporting well, things are progressing well, and the government wants to continue its policy of not frightening the market," Manoel Bertone, vice-president of the National Coffee Council, told reporters after a meeting of private sector coffee representatives.
Brazilian growers have in recent months demanded the government increase the size and frequency of its stock sales in order to ease tight domestic supply.

A government official last week said coffee stocks should ideally be between five and six million bags, compared to 13.8 million bags at present, but he did not say when and how current stocks would be reduced outside of the regular sales.
Bertone said growers, exporters and soluble industry officials were working together on a global plan to restructure the domestic coffee industry which would satisfy every sector's interests.
They discussed a request from growers for shorter credit periods in order to counterbalance what they said were "too elastic" payment periods for domestic coffee.
Conditions for selling the new crop were good with Brazil's production falling and international supply tight.
"International availability is really low. Brazil at this point will have a good opportunity for selling this year's harvest (at a good price)," Bertone said.
The government has said it is working with an estimate of between 18 and 22 million 60-kg bags for the 1997/98 crop.

But talks about a possible sale of government coffee stocks to the soluble industry, which says it is having trouble competing with industries abroad because of high domestic prices, had stopped short at the question of prices.
"We need to discuss the level of prices in relation to London," Bertone said. "London has to be the parameter, otherwise it won't be solved."
